desc: Derive bounds: prove d = x-y satisfies d³ < N so d ≤ 10⁶, and that d must divide N.
Implement integer cube root of N (via round(N ** (1/3)) with adjustment) to cap the enumeration loop.
Loop d from 1 to cbrt(N); skip if N % d != 0; compute m = N // d.
For each (d, m), compute discriminant D = 12m - 3d²; check D ≥ 0, perfect square via integer isqrt, and y = (-3d + sqrt(D)) / 6 is a positive integer.
On first valid pair, print x = y + d and y; if loop finishes, print -1.
Write final Python solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin), verify against samples 397 → "12 11", 1 → "-1", and the large sample.
